newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil again denies report Loyola to resign.
newsitem.headline: Brazil again denies report Loyola to resign.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola has no immediate plans to resign and the government has no wish to see him go, an aide to Finance Minister Pedro Malan said.
"He has no wish to resign and the government no desire to see him go," the aide told Reuters, vigorously and angrily dismissing a report in the Correio Brasiliense newspaper.

The Correio report was based on unnamed sources in the Presidency and the Finance Ministry and follows market rumors mid-week that Loyola had handed in his resignation. Malan's aide dismissed the talk as "lies".
"I will bet you a bottle of champagne that Loyola does not resign," he said.
Bolsa traders said the report had had no impact and was considered a slightly tardy follow-up to the rumors earlier in the week.

Loyola, who has been periodically dogged by speculation that he is uncomfortable in his role as Central Bank chief and would prefer a private sector position, himself denied there was any truth to those rumors.
